To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Hsps are able to cross‐prime CTLs against multiple tumor antigens, (2) Hsps can induce CTL responses in the absence of TAP molecules, (3) DCs internalize Hsps, (4) peptides derived from Hsps can be re‐presented via the MHC I pathway by DCs, and (5) the cross‐priming of CTLs is dependent on the presence and function of DCs.
Hsp70‐pulsing DCs can be used to elicit CTLs against multiple tumor‐associated antigenic epitopes in a TAP‐dependent fashion.
tumor‐derived Hsp70‐pulsedin DCs elicit tumor‐derived CTLs and tumor immunity in a TAP‐dependent manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of new therapeutic strategies against cancer.
the development of novel immunotherapies for the treatment of cancer.
the development of novel immunotherapeutic strategies against cancer, based on the exploitation of tumor‐derived Hsps as a means of generating tumor‐specific CTLs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Hsp‐pulsed bone marrow‐derived DCs are able to induce a potent CTL response against the tumor antigen, which is presented in a TAP‐dependent manner.
the HSPs are not the most important ones in the development of the HSPs.
tumor‐derived Hsp70‐pulsing DCs elicit tumor‐antigen specific CTLs and that this is mediated through a TAP‐dependent MHC class I presentation pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Hsp70 is a powerful antigen‐loading molecule that can efficiently load peptides into the MHC class I presentation pathway, and that Hsp70‐pulsing DCs are capable of eliciting CTL responses against multiple antigen‐peptides in a TAP‐dependent manner.
we have shown that HSP70 can be used as an effective immunogen to induce tumor‐specific cytolytic T lymphocyte (CTL) responses.

we have shown that tumor-derived heat shock proteins can be taken up by DCs in a receptor-dependent manner, and that they are able to elicit strong cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) responses in a TAP-dependent manner, which is the first step in the generation of tumor-specific CTLs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HSP‐peptides can be internalized by APCs, processed and presented by MHC molecules.
Hsp70‐pulsing DCs can induce CTLs against multiple tumor‐associated antigens in a TAP‐dependent manner.
Hsp70 can be used as an adjuvant to induce CTL responses.
